title: Can a penalty hold the cartel together?

predict.q: A cartel agrees a **penalty** that any member caught cheating must pay; it is taken off the cheater's payoff. Which is the smallest penalty on the slider that makes keeping to the quota a dominant strategy?

options.fb: At 30, cheating still pays whatever the rival does: 845 > 800 and 720 > 700.
At 60, cheating still pays when the rival keeps to quota (815 > 800). Keeping is best only if the rival cheats, so it is not dominant.
At 90 cheating pays less in both columns (785 < 800, 660 < 700): keeping is dominant.
120 works, but it is not the smallest: at 90, cheating already pays less in both columns (785 < 800, 660 < 700).

task: Move the penalty slider and watch the cheat payoffs and the ticked best responses.

target.do: Move the penalty slider, then press Check.

takeaway: Keeping to the quota is dominant only when cheating pays less **whatever** the rival does: here a penalty above 75.
